The 39-year-old, who also failed to make the 2017 edition due to a elbow injury, needed a run to the semi-finals to keep himself in with a chance of clinching a spot at the season-ending showpiece in Turin. Campbell was face down on the turf and not moving after hitting tight end TJ Hockenson early in the fourth quarter of the Lions' 19-15 victory on Sunday. The 26-year-old was evaluated by medical personnel before being strapped to a board and carefully lifted onto the cart to a round of applause. Substitutes Gatlin O'Donkor and Mo Missanga struck twice in eight minutes to earn Oxford a 2-0 victory over local rivals Reading and a first Thames Valley derby win since 1999. Just minutes after coming off the bench, O'Donkor thundered a low left-footed shot from Cameron Brannagan's free-kick in off the far post to delight the home fans in a packed Kassam Stadium. After that 71st-minute breakthrough, Missanga then turned in O'Donkor's knock-down at a corner in the 78th minute to seal the three points. Victory extended the U's unbeaten run to 10 games and lifted Aaron Ramsey's men to third in League One. Although Reading had their chances, United - who controlled a lot of the possession - deserved the win. Brannagan twice went close at free-kicks and visiting goalkeeper Joel Pereira also made a fine smothering save

messages.text: Leicestershire's relegation stands as points deduction for 'poor' pitch upheld

metadata.summary: Leicestershire's relegation to County Championship Division Two has been confirmed after the club's points deduction for breaching pitch regulations was upheld.
metadata.content: Leicestershire's County Championship relegation confirmed as points deduction for 'poor' pitch upheld | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Leicestershire's County Championship relegation confirmed as points deduction for 'poor' pitch upheld Leicestershire join Hampshire in being relegated from Division One; Foxes argued that state of pitch for victory over Glamorgan had been due to shooting of Bollywood film days before fixture; Leicestershire finish 17 points behind third-bottom Essex in table as 19-point sanction stands Wednesday 4 November 2026 20:09, UK Image: Leicestershire's relegation to County Championship Division Two has been confirmed after the club's points deduction for breaching pitch regulations was upheld Leicestershire's relegation to County Championship Division Two has been confirmed after the club's points deduction for breaching pitch regulations was upheld. The Foxes were hit with a 27-point penalty, later cut to 19, after the surface at Grace Road was rated "poor" by the match referee following the win over Glamorgan in August. Leicestershire, who argued the state of the pitch was due to the unscheduled shooting of a Bollywood film days before the Glamorgan fixture, had eight points from the original punishment of 27 reinstated but then appealed against the 19-point sanction.
